guided.title: Check the grain
guided.prompt: The block builds the warehouse. Replace the last query so that it returns one row with the columns `lines` (rows in `fact_sales`) and `distinct_sales` (distinct `sale_id`).
hints: Both numbers come from `fact_sales` in one query.
`SELECT count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT sale_id) AS distinct_sales FROM fact_sales`.

guided.title: Revenue by category
guided.prompt: Return `category` and `amount_cents` (sum of the fact's `amount_cents`) for every product category, ordered by `category`, by joining `fact_sales` to `dim_product` on `product_key`.
hints: The fact table is the left table of the join.
Group by the category column of the dimension.
`JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_key = f.product_key GROUP BY p.category`.

guided.title: The correct average price
guided.prompt: Return one row per `month` of `dim_date` (join on `date_key`) with the columns `month` and `avg_price_cents`, where `avg_price_cents` is `sum(amount_cents) / sum(quantity)` rounded to 1 decimal (cast to numeric first), ordered by `month`.
hints: A ratio is computed from two sums.
Cast one sum to `numeric` so that the division is not an integer division.

guided.title: Units per country
guided.prompt: Join `fact_sales` to `dim_customer` and return `country` and `units` (sum of `quantity`) ordered by `country`.
hints: The country is in the customer dimension.

independent.title: Best category per month
independent.prompt: For each month of `dim_date`, return the category with the highest `amount_cents` that month: columns `month`, `category`, `amount_cents`, ordered by `month`. (Use a CTE with sums per month and category and `rank()` or `DISTINCT ON`; there are no ties in this data.)

independent.title: A fan-out you can measure
independent.prompt: The table `promo(product_key, promo_name)` lists product 1 twice and product 2 once. Return one row with `true_total` (sum of `amount_cents` of products 1 and 2 from `fact_sales`) and `joined_total` (the same sum after joining `fact_sales` to `promo` on `product_key`).

independent.title: Declare a grain
independent.prompt: Choose a process (support tickets, deliveries or library loans). Write the grain sentence, three dimensions, two measures and say whether each measure is additive.
independent.solution: Process: deliveries. Grain: one row per parcel delivered. Dimensions: date delivered, customer, carrier (also destination region if parcels have one). Measures: `weight_grams` (additive across all dimensions) and `delivery_minutes` (additive as a sum, but reported as an average computed as sum divided by the number of parcels; a stored `on_time_percent` would be non-additive and is computed from counts instead). Each row has one date, one customer and one carrier, which confirms the grain: nothing in the dimension list has several values per parcel.
rubric: States the grain as one sentence
Lists dimensions that each take one value at that grain
Classifies measures and avoids a stored ratio

checks.question: What is the grain of `fact_sales` in the warehouse used here?
checks.explanation: Each row is one product bought by one customer on one date; that statement is the grain. The other options describe aggregates built from it.

checks.question: Why is `sum(amount_cents) / sum(quantity)` a better average price than `avg(amount_cents / quantity)`?
options: It weights each unit equally instead of each order line equally
checks.explanation: Averaging per-row prices treats a one-unit line like a fifty-unit line. The ratio of sums is the true average price per unit.

checks.question: A query joins `fact_sales` to a table with two rows for product 1. What happens to the sum for product 1?
checks.explanation: Every fact row for product 1 matches two rows, so it appears twice. The join changed the grain of the result.

checks.question: Which belongs in a dimension table?
checks.explanation: Country is a descriptive attribute used to group and filter. Quantity and amount are measures; the sale id identifies a fact row.

checks.question: Why declare the grain before choosing columns?
options: It decides which dimensions and measures make sense and prevents mixing rows at different levels
checks.explanation: Dimensions and measures are valid only at the declared grain. Most modelling errors come from rows of different grain sharing a table.
